questions.question: How can you help reduce road rage?

options.text: Always signal before changing lanes.
Talk on your cell phone while driving.
Use your horn frequently.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, follow all traffic laws, signs, signals, and road markings. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: Which of these commonly causes traffic crashes?

options.text: Speeding or driving too fast for road conditions.
Getting adequate rest and staying alert.
Paying attention to your surroundings and focusing on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speeding or driving too fast for road conditions.
questions.explanation: Speeding and driving too fast for conditions cause many crashes. Always drive at legal speeds and adjust your speed based on traffic and weather.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must yield to you.
Never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic going straight. You must always yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: You see pedestrians near the road. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and keep your speed.
Speed up to get past them quickly.
Slow down and pass with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and pass with caution.
questions.explanation: Watch for pedestrians who might cross your path. If you see pedestrians near the road, slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Look only straight ahead.
Focus only on the middle of the road.
Watch all directions: ahead, to the sides, and behind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch all directions: ahead, to the sides, and behind.
questions.explanation: A good driver watches all around their car. You need to know what is happening in every direction.

questions.question: Is it legal to drive while taking medication that affects your driving?

options.text: No, never.
Yes, if you don't feel drowsy.
Yes, if a doctor prescribed it.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive under the influence of any substance that affects your driving. This includes alcohol, prescription drugs, over-the-counter drugs, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: How can you spot an aggressive driver?

options.text: They make sudden and improper lane changes.
They have many passengers in their car.
They drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make sudden and improper lane changes.
questions.explanation: Watch for drivers making sudden or improper lane changes. Do not challenge aggressive drivers. The safest option is to stay away from them.

questions.question: What are the fines for speeding in work zones?

options.text: They can be twice as much as normal speeding fines.
They are usually not enforced.
You can always argue them in court.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can be twice as much as normal speeding fines.
questions.explanation: In Connecticut, speeding in a work zone can result in fines up to $1,000, points on your license, and required driver retraining. Distracted driving fines are doubled in work zones.

questions.question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if pedestrians wave at you first.
Only if pedestrians are not using their phones.
Always.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always.
questions.explanation: Stop completely at a crosswalk to yield to any pedestrian. You may proceed only when your lane is completely clear.

questions.question: What can happen if you take a prescription drug and drink alcohol together?

options.text: There will probably be no effect.
It will make you more alert.
It can make you unsafe to drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can make you unsafe to drive.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter medications can affect your driving ability. They are especially dangerous when combined with alcohol.

questions.question: In rain or fog, drivers should use their:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain, snow, sleet, or fog. High beams reflect off wet surfaces and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: When driving behind a large truck on the freeway, you should drive:

options.text: Closer behind the truck than you would a passenger vehicle.
Farther behind the truck than you would a passenger vehicle.
To the right side of the truck and wait to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther behind the truck than you would a passenger vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have bigger blind spots. You need to stay farther back than you would behind a regular car.

questions.question: Before returning to your lane after passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Beep your horn.
See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
Flash your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You can safely return to your lane only when you see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: What is the only proven way to remove alcohol or drugs from your system?

options.text: Breathe fresh air.
Give your body time.
Drink coffee.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give your body time.
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your system. Cold showers, coffee, and exercise do not lower your blood alcohol level.

questions.question: A pedestrian with a guide dog is crossing in front of you at a corner. You want to turn right. You should:

options.text: Turn off your engine until the person crosses.
Tell the pedestrian when to cross.
Wait until the person crosses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the person crosses.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians with guide dogs or white canes always have the right-of-way. Let them cross before you turn.

questions.question: A solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal means:

options.text: Speed up to make the turn before the light changes.
You do not need to signal when turning from that lane.
Prepare to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the green turn protection is ending. Get ready to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before turning.

questions.question: Alcohol and drugs affect which of these driving skills?

options.text: Alertness.
Coordination.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs harm reaction time, coordination, alertness, and concentration—all skills needed for safe driving.

questions.question: The best way to change lanes is:

options.text: Quickly and often.
When a car is in your blind spot.
Gradually and carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gradually and carefully.
questions.explanation: Always change lanes gradually and carefully. Change lanes only when needed. Every lane change increases the risk of an accident.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, you should:

options.text: Follow the driver in front of you closely.
Pass the driver in front of you as soon as possible.
Stay a safe distance behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay a safe distance behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: In work zones, keep a safe distance from barriers, equipment, workers, and other vehicles. Do not tailgate.

questions.question: As you enter a roundabout, you should slow down and:

options.text: Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists.
Yield to cars already in the roundabout.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and all traffic already in the roundabout.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Motorist services.
Construction and maintenance.
Mileage information, such as distances to specific locations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorist services.
questions.explanation: Blue signs provide information about services for drivers. These signs show where you can find rest areas, food, or hospitals.

questions.question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to:

options.text: Make drivers angry about slow traffic.
Inconvenience drivers.
Keep traffic out of hazardous work zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep traffic out of hazardous work zones.
questions.explanation: Work zones are dangerous for both workers and drivers. Watch for cones, barrels, signs, large vehicles, and workers in bright vests. These warn you and show you where to go.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a steep hill ahead.
No trucks are allowed on the upcoming hill.
A logging road is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you of a steep hill ahead. Slow down and be ready to control your speed to protect your brakes.

questions.question: What is a crosswalk?

options.text: Another name for a four-way intersection.
An area designated for road construction workers.
The area where pedestrians may cross the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: The area where pedestrians may cross the roadway.
questions.explanation: Crosswalks are often marked with white lines to show where people can cross. Some crosswalks have extra lines between them, and some have no marks at all.

questions.question: If you come to a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing warning lights, you should:

options.text: Drive around the crossing gates if you can't see a train.
Come to a complete stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, and proceed once the gates are lifted.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, and proceed once the gates are lifted.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing if there are warning signs, flashing lights, or flaggers. It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.
